_README: Committed baseline for the memory verification suite (v3).
Gated by tests/memverify/test_o_baseline.py via tests/memverify/metrics.py.
Each entry is {"min": n} or {"max": n}. A bound of null means the number
has NEVER been measured; that is reported as a FAILURE, not tolerated, and
the failure message prints the JSON to paste back here. A number nobody has
looked at must not read as a pass.
`source` records where a bound came from, so a modelled figure can never be
mistaken for a measured one:
contract  - restates an assertion the suite already makes elsewhere.
invariant - follows from the production code, not from a measurement.
measured  - observed on a real run; `recorded_at` names that run.
unrecorded- bound is null; the next real run must record it.
════ 2026-08-21 — MEASURED AGAINST A LIVE MODEL ════
The 2026-08-20 note below this line said the v3 suite had never been run
against a live model, because the key in backend/.env answers 401. That is
still true LOCALLY. It is no longer true of the suite: CI carries a working
key and has now run it eight times, and every headline number in this file
comes from those runs.
What the live runs found, none of which the deterministic half could:
* The prompt's own teaching EXHIBIT was being copied into a user's
memory verbatim - a tutor's name and an invented date range that
appeared nowhere in the conversation. Fixed structurally
(`memory_curator.leaked_exhibit`), not just by rewording.
* The writer answered four turns with `update_description` and stored
NOTHING. Capture 66.67%. A description rewrite is the one op that can
spend a turn's whole budget while recording nothing.
* A wholly Persian turn produced an English bullet.
* A music taste went to you/profile with no topics file.
* A `create_file` slug written without its `people/` prefix was refused,
and the refusal cascaded through the seven ops that depended on it.
And three defects in this SUITE, each of which scored correct curation as
wrong: `find_capture` reported the first match in dict order rather than
preferring the routed one; P07 demanded two facts in one bullet; and two
markers (P02, P06) demanded the exact spellings the house voice forbids -
a first-person Persian verb, and a person's name inside their own file.
THE DISCIPLINE THIS FILE ASKS FOR IS STILL NOT FULLY MET. It wants three
CONSECUTIVE clean-state runs before a bound is recorded. Every run so far
sat on a different build, because each one was read and then fixed. The
`misroute_pct` bound below is therefore a ceiling chosen from two runs on
the shipped writer and reasoned about, not a three-run measurement. Re-run
it three times unchanged and tighten it.
════ Why the metric SET changed ════
The row-era metrics are gone with the row engine and the old numbers are
NOT comparable, so they were not adjusted; they were replaced.
recall_pct         -> capture_pct     (same question, file-shaped: a
fact must be in ONE BULLET of the
LABELED FILE, not merely stored)
precision_pct      -> precision_pct   (unchanged in meaning)
unlabeled_rate_pct -> lint_clean_pct  + misroute_pct
unlabeled_rate_pct measured the share of stored ROWS whose `category`
column carried no usable label. It had a MEASURED ceiling of 8.0% because
the label came from an LLM and the number jittered across seven runs.
Neither the column nor the jitter survives: v3 has no per-row category,
and two of the three replacements are deterministic —
* lint_clean_pct — a bullet not in the house voice, or a description
that does not match DESCRIPTION_RE. The lint runs INSIDE
`validate_ops`, so a non-zero rate does not mean the model wrote badly;
it means something reached a body without going through the ops engine.
Structural, so the bound is an invariant, not a tolerance.
* misroute_pct — a captured fact in the wrong file. Root cause #3 of the
rebuild, and structurally invisible to the row corpus, which could only
ask whether text was stored somewhere. This one IS the model's
judgement, so it is the one bound that must be measured rather than
argued — hence null until a real run records it.
════ The fixture to watch ════
B21 is RED on main under the row extractor (verified independently on
cd24717b and 52dbd3ab): the assistant sentence "You should avoid ebi,
kani, and anything with a shellfish-based broth..." — a CONDITIONAL, in
the ASSISTANT's voice, about an allergy the user does not have — was
stored as a fact. Two independent v3 guards must refuse it: the assistant
block is labelled context-only, and advice/hypotheticals are named in
TURN_DURABILITY_RULES. It is carried here verbatim so the first live run
settles whether v3 turns that lane green.

capture_pct.note: test_a_capture_recall.py::test_capture_rate already asserts every labeled fact is in its labeled file; 100% is the same statement. Restated here so all four headline numbers are gated in one place. NOT yet confirmed by a live run - see _README.

precision_pct.note: test_b_precision_junk.py::test_junk_rate_is_zero_across_the_WHOLE_corpus already asserts zero junk across every scenario, belt runs included; 100% precision is the same statement as a junk count of 0. NOT yet confirmed by a live run - see _README.

lint_clean_pct.note: Every bullet and description that reaches a body passes through memory_file_ops.validate_ops, which runs bullet_problem and description_problem and rejects the op otherwise. A lint failure in a stored body therefore means a write path bypassed the ops engine - a structural defect, not a quality judgement, so the bound follows from the code rather than from a sample.

misroute_pct.recorded_at: CI 32433614861 (0.0) and 32434234265 (8.33), both on the shipped writer; the trend across the whole rebuild was 22.22 -> 12.5 -> 9.09 -> 9.09 -> 8.33 -> 0.0 -> 8.33
misroute_pct.note: A CEILING, not the measurement, and deliberately so. The corpus carries 12 capture markers, so ONE misrouted fact is 8.33% and there is no value between 0 and 8.33 to sit on. Recording 0.0 would fail the suite on a single stochastic miss by a model that is judged, not computed; recording 8.33 would pin the bound to the exact count of today's corpus and silently loosen every time a marker is added. 10.0 catches a real regression (two misroutes is 16.7%) and tolerates one. Tighten it if the corpus grows: the bound should stay just above 1/N.
